segments.text: Welcome to the Robotics News Digest for November 13, 2026.
Today we cover Agile Robots' funding, XPENG's UK expansion, and Viam Launchpad's deployment goals.
Stay informed.
From Humanoid.guide, Agile Robots raises five hundred million dollars at an eight point five billion valuation.
This report details the recent financing round and the subsequent strategic plans for the company.
Agile Robots secured five hundred million dollars in a Series F funding round, establishing an eight point five billion valuation for the firm.
The capital is designated for United States expansion, increased production capacity within Germany, and broader market entry initiatives.
The company has deployed more than twenty thousand robotic solutions across diverse industrial sectors.
Production targets are set for 2027, differentiating between large legged and wheeled humanoids, alongside smaller research models.
The Agile ONE SN integrates Nvidia technology for research applications and is projected for availability in early 2027.
This development indicates continued investment and expansion within the advanced robotics and artificial intelligence sector.
From Robotics & Automation News, XPENG expands UK operations with new vehicles, robotaxis and humanoid robots.
This report details XPENG's expansion strategy in the United Kingdom focusing on vehicle introduction and the development of physical artificial intelligence systems.
XPENG intends to introduce five new right-hand-drive models within twelve months, concentrating on intelligent driving technology and dual-energy solutions across the expanded market.
The company plans to establish a nationwide network comprising one hundred retail and service locations and secure twenty key partnerships by the year twenty twenty seven.

Furthermore, XPENG is developing a wider physical AI ecosystem encompassing Robotaxi services and humanoid robots with the objective of becoming the United Kingdom's leading premium electric vehicle brand by twenty twenty eight through a focus on customer experience.
This development signals increasing integration of physical AI into automotive and robotics sectors.
From The Robot Report, Viam Launchpad aims to accelerate robotics deployments.

This report details how Viam provides a software platform functioning as an abstraction layer for building and deploying hardware systems, enabling robotics startups to move rapidly from prototypes to market.
The platform furnishes the necessary infrastructure to help founders overcome obstacles in building and deploying physical artificial intelligence by providing essential resources.
Viam Launchpad offers an intensive program that includes technical support, resources, and access to hardware labs to facilitate commercial implementation.
The platform has already assisted companies such as Gambit in achieving real-world deployments by streamlining the process of connecting hardware with software.
Ultimately, Viam seeks to expedite the deployment of physical AI by reducing the barriers for robotics entrepreneurs.
This development signals an effort to increase the pace of physical AI commercialization across the technology sector.
From Humanoid.guide, GXO targets 1,000 Apptronik Apollo robots, Koetsier reports.

This report details GXO Logistics' agreement with Apptronik for the deployment of up to one thousand Apollo humanoids beginning in twenty twenty seven, with an estimated cost of fifteen dollars per hour for the units.

The proposed deployment encompasses tasks such as picking, packing, and sorting goods inside warehouses, emphasizing requirements for dexterity, reliable manipulation, speed, uptime, and autonomy in the robotic systems.
GXO has previously completed over forty five humanoid pilots across different suppliers as part of their evaluation process.
This development signals increased industrial interest in applying advanced humanoid robotics for complex logistical operations.
From thesequence.substack.com, The Sequence Robotics - Issue 971 reports on a method for robots to learn through on-the-job experience guided by remote human tutors.
This research involves using real-world work interventions as training data to improve robot intelligence.
The system incorporates a research fleet of one hundred robots and a process termed TRACE, which facilitates a real-to-sim-to-real loop for additional practice.
The development aims to establish an apprenticeship model where the work itself forms part of the learning curriculum.
Core investigation centers on the efficacy of real-world practice and the reliability of simulated learning outcomes.
This work suggests a pathway toward integrating practical experience directly into robotic training protocols.
The findings indicate a method for enhancing machine learning through contextual, real-world application.
Future developments will focus on scaling this apprenticeship model across various industrial applications.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, Pelican Unify 1.0!".

This report details the release of Pelican Unify 1.0, an embodied AI foundation model residing in the software layer of robotics, which currently holds a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of five out of ten, marking it as an emerging software offering.
The model was developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, known as X Humanoid, and was released on May 14, 2026.
It functions as an embodied AI foundation model operating within the software layer rather than physical hardware.
The current availability of the model is backorder, and prospective users are advised to evaluate the model independently from complete robotic systems when considering its application.
Further specific details regarding the model are accessible on the official source.
The introduction of this software-based foundation model signifies continued development in embodied artificial intelligence within the robotics sector.
From Humanoid.guide, "Welcome, LingBot-Touch!".
This segment reports on LingBot Touch, a software foundation model developed by Robbyant focused specifically on tactile data.
The model was trained on nearly five thousand hours of touch recordings from gloves and robot hands, establishing tactile data as central to its identity.
This model is designed to complement other robot software rather than act as an independent controller, achieving a Humanoid Guide Brain Score of five out of ten.
The development highlights the growing research focus on integrating tactile data within embodied artificial intelligence systems.
Future developments in embodied AI systems are anticipated to continue focusing on rich sensory input.
From MIT News - Robotics, "Helping robots fit into the human workplace".
This report details the development of robust artificial intelligence designed to complement human capabilities in factory and warehouse environments.
The company has developed mobile robots, such as Carter, featuring force-sensitive handlebars and artificial intelligence vision to facilitate intuitive human control.
The development philosophy centers on creating systems where human agency and input guide the operational process.
These robots are deployed to assist with tasks including picking, stocking, and moving items within logistics and manufacturing settings.
The methodology prioritizes accelerating human tasks rather than outright replacement.
This research indicates a trend toward collaborative robotics integration in industrial settings.
The continued development of such systems suggests an increased focus on human-robot collaboration across various sectors.
And that's all the circuits for today's dive into the world of robotics.
Agile Robots is really setting the pace!
Thanks for tuning in; keep those algorithms humming!
See you tomorrow.
